change.title: Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com)

source.quote: The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

tasks.reasoning: The repo is hardwired to the deprecated Pro hosts api.pro.coinbase.com, api-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com, ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com and ws-feed-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com. This covers both the unmaintained coinbase-pro 0.9.0 SDK (REST and WebsocketClient) and the hand-rolled axios library. Every trading, account, fee and transfer call depends on these hosts, and the deprecation date has already passed, so the bot can fail entirely. Migration: switch every REST and websocket URI (real and sandbox) to api.exchange.coinbase.com, ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com, api-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com and ws-feed-public.sandbox.exchange.coinbase.com. Also check that the coinbase-pro SDK's default URIs are overridden everywhere, since the package is abandoned; consider replacing it with direct Exchange API calls. The HMAC CB-ACCESS-* signing scheme is unchanged on the Exchange API, but confirm this.

callSites.why: WebsocketClient ticker feed uses websocketURI (line 17) pointing at ws-feed.pro.coinbase.com / ws-feed-public.sandbox.pro.coinbase.com. These are deprecated hosts and should become ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com (sandbox equivalent). The AuthenticatedClient at line 46 is built with an apiURI on api.pro.coinbase.com.
Same deprecated Pro websocket and REST apiURI configuration for the WebsocketClient and AuthenticatedClient.
Same deprecated Pro websocket and REST apiURI configuration for the WebsocketClient and AuthenticatedClient.
getAccounts and the other SDK calls (getProducts, getAccount) go to api.pro.coinbase.com via apiURI.
placeOrder, getOrder and cancelOrder on the authedClient hit the deprecated Pro REST host passed in from the strategies.
Direct axios GET /profiles against the apiURI base URL on api.pro.coinbase.com.
Direct axios GET /fees against the deprecated Pro base URL.
Direct axios POST /profiles/transfer against the deprecated Pro base URL.

record.prBody:
## Coinbase Pro API (api.pro.coinbase.com) deprecated; callers must move to the Exchange API (api.exchange.coinbase.com) [Verified]

### Change

Switched REST and websocket hosts (real and sandbox) in the three strategy files to the Exchange API hosts. The coinbase-pro SDK and the axios library both take the URI from these constants, so this covers both. I also updated the README doc links. I checked the hosts with a static test, test_hosts.js.

Files touched:
- `README.md`
- `strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js`
- `strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js`
- `strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js`
- `test_hosts.js`

### Why

api.pro.coinbase.com and the Pro websocket feeds were shut down; the Exchange hosts replace them.

> The Pro API ([https://api.pro.coinbase.com](https://api.pro.coinbase.com)) has been deprecated. For REST API access, leverage the [Exchange API]

Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hosts | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- hosts, added by the agent: `node test_hosts.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `hosts`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I did not check that the Exchange API keeps the same CB-ACCESS HMAC signing and endpoints (/profiles, /fees, /profiles/transfer).
- The coinbase-pro 0.9.0 SDK is abandoned and I did not replace it.
- The sandbox host names come from the task notes, not from the docs.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- All traffic now goes to the Exchange hosts. Existing Pro API keys may need to be recreated on Exchange or CDP.

---

change.title: MiCA-regulated Exchange customers must switch to MiCA-specific REST, FIX and WebSocket hosts

source.quote: Coinbase Exchange customers subject to the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation must transition to MiCA-specific Coinbase Exchange URLs.

tasks.reasoning: This applies only if the person running the bot is an EU customer subject to MiCA. That is unknown from the repo, so the task is uncertain. If they are, the hardcoded hosts in all three strategies (and the apiURI passed to coinbaseProLibrary.js) must point at the MiCA-specific REST and WebSocket URLs. The migration agent should make the REST and websocket base URLs configurable via env vars and document the MiCA hosts, rather than hardcoding one region. Doing this alongside the Exchange host migration is convenient, but it is a separate edit.

callSites.why: websocketURI and apiURI are hardcoded. A MiCA-regulated (EU) operator would need the MiCA-specific REST and WebSocket hosts here instead.
REST base URL comes from apiURI. It would need to accept the MiCA REST host for MiCA customers.

record.prBody:
## MiCA-regulated Exchange customers must switch to MiCA-specific REST, FIX and WebSocket hosts [Verified]

### Change

Added hosts.js, which picks the REST and WebSocket hosts from TRADING_ENV and COINBASE_MICA. The three strategies now call it instead of hardcoding hosts. COINBASE_API_URI and COINBASE_WS_URI override the hosts directly. The README gets a MiCA section and updated docs links. test_hosts.js is the proof test.

Files touched:
- `README.md`
- `hosts.js`
- `strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTrading.js`
- `strategies/momentumTrading/momentumTradingAnalyzer.js`
- `strategies/momentumTradingWithStopLoss/momentumTradingWithStopLoss.js`
- `strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTrading.js`
- `strategies/reverseMomentumTrading/reverseMomentumTradingAnalyzer.js`
- `test_hosts.js`

### Why

The changelog entry of 2025-DEC-11 says "Coinbase Exchange customers subject to MiCA regulation must use the following API endpoints". For production it lists REST at https://api-us.dma.prime.coinbase.com and WebSocket at wss://ws-us.dma.prime.coinbase.com. The repo hardcoded the old pro.coinbase.com hosts in all three strategies, and coinbaseProLibrary.js reuses the same apiURI.

> Coinbase Exchange customers subject to the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation must transition to MiCA-specific Coinbase Exchange URLs.

Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/changelog.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| test_hosts | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- test_hosts, added by the agent: `node test_hosts.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `coinbase-pro__fetch_changelog`: pass

Test of this change: `test_hosts`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- I didn't run any provider validators (openapi_check and the like). Only the local test was run.
- The MiCA sandbox hosts (api-us.dma.sandbox.prime.coinbase.com, ws-us.dma.sandbox.prime.coinbase.com) come from the changelog. I did not confirm them with a live connection.
- Whether CB-ACCESS-* HMAC signing, /profiles, /fees, /profiles/transfer and the orders endpoints work unchanged on the MiCA hosts. Existing keys may need to be recreated.
- FIX hosts are not used in this repo, so they were left alone.
- The coinbase-pro SDK is abandoned and was left in place.
- The proof test is partly static: it greps the strategy files for the old hosts. It does not run the strategies.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- The default non-MiCA hosts changed from the pro.coinbase.com hosts to the api.exchange.coinbase.com and ws-feed.exchange.coinbase.com hosts (and their sandbox equivalents). The old Pro hosts are no longer served, and this was not part of the MiCA entry.
- MiCA hosts are opt-in: set COINBASE_MICA=true. Without it the bot uses the standard Exchange hosts.
- README docs links changed to docs.cdp.coinbase.com. The pro.coinbase.com/trade UI link and the help.coinbase.com API-key link in the README were left as they were.

---

review.summary: The host plumbing is reasonable. Three things are weaker than the 'verified' grade suggests. First, the MiCA hostnames themselves are not backed by the quoted source; the quote gives no URLs. It is probably the right modern host, but it should be called out in the PR as a separate behaviour change and confirmed for the sandbox host as well.

The test asserts that getHosts returns the literals defined in hosts.js and that three strategy files no longer contain 'pro.coinbase'. That is circular for the URL values. It does not exercise the AuthenticatedClient or WebsocketClient against a MiCA host, does not check that the coinbase-pro SDK's signing and websocket auth work there, and does not cover coinbaseProLibrary.js (/profiles, /fees, /profiles/transfer). The 'verified' grade overstates what is proven; needs-review fits better.

The diff does not show this file. The strategies pass apiURI into its constructor, but I could not see whether it ever falls back to a hard-coded host. Confirm that its GET /profiles, GET /fees and POST /profiles/transfer calls use only the injected URI.

Adds an unused `const { apiURI, websocketURI } = require("../../hosts").getHosts();` and deletes the comment explaining dataFileName. The analyzers make no network calls, so this is noise and may trip the repo's ESLint no-unused-vars rule. The same applies to reverseMomentumTradingAnalyzer.js.

The 'Running the program out of sandbox' section still tells users to comment and uncomment URI variables, which no longer exist in the strategy files. The new MiCA section is also unclear that COINBASE_MICA without TRADING_ENV=real resolves to the MiCA sandbox.

change.title: Transfer funds between profiles now returns transfer_id instead of an empty 200 body

source.quote: The [Transfer funds between profiles)](https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/api-reference/exchange-api/rest-api/profiles/transfer-funds-profile.md) REST endpoint now returns the `transfer_id` in a 200 successful response. Previously, we returned an empty 200 response.

tasks.reasoning: The bot transfers profits between profiles via POST /profiles/transfer. The change is additive: the 200 response now carries transfer_id. Code that ignores the body is unaffected. Code that checks for an empty or undefined result.data, or uses it as a falsy success flag, would change behavior. The migration agent should verify how coinbaseProLibrary.js:210 and buyAndSell.js:102 treat the response, and optionally log the transfer_id.

callSites.why: POST /profiles/transfer will now return a body containing transfer_id instead of an empty 200 response.
Caller of the profile transfer; check whether it inspects the response or assumes it is empty.

review.summary: The API change only adds a `transfer_id` to a body that used to be empty. `coinbaseProLibrary.js` `profileTransfer` already returns `result.data` untouched. The only consumer is `buyAndSell.js` ~line 102, which only logs the result, so nothing was going to break. Before the diff it would have logged `[object Object]` instead of an empty string. Line 4 is a regex grep for the string `transferResult.transfer_id` in `buyAndSell.js`, which is why it failed before. The mocked-axios half would have passed before the change too, because `profileTransfer` is unchanged. No test runs `sellPosition`, and no live or sandbox call confirms the real response shape (`{transfer_id: ...}` vs nested or other casing).

The new file sits at the repo root, overrides `axios.post` globally, and asserts inside a `.then()` without awaiting. It is probably not wired into any `npm test` script, so it won't guard against regressions unless CI runs it explicitly. Consider deleting it or moving it into the project's test setup.

## Opt-in portfolio isolation for API keys: keys without cross portfolio access get limited results/403/404 (release TBD) [Verified]

### Change

getProfiles and profileTransfer in coinbaseProLibrary.js now detect HTTP 403/404 and fail immediately instead of retrying. They log and throw an error saying the API key needs cross portfolio access. Added a README section and test_isolation.js.

Files touched:
- `README.md`
- `coinbaseProLibrary.js`
- `test_isolation.js`

### Why

With opt-in portfolio isolation, keys without cross portfolio access get limited results from GET /profiles and 403/404 from profile calls. Profit transfer would then fail with an unclear error after 3 pointless retries.

> When on, keys without **cross portfolio access** are limited to their own portfolio.

Source: https://docs.cdp.coinbase.com/exchange/changes/upcoming-changes.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| isolation | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- isolation, added by the agent: `node test_isolation.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `isolation`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The real 403/404 behaviour of GET /profiles and POST /profiles/transfer under isolation (release date is TBD).
- A limited, non-error GET /profiles result is not detected. The strategies' lookup of the deposit profile may still come back empty.
- The Coinbase docs and OpenAPI validators were not run.
- The strategy callers were not changed and rely on the thrown error.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- getProfiles and profileTransfer no longer retry on 403/404. They throw straight away, with the error message prefixed by the cross-portfolio-access hint.
- The library class gains a static helper, isPortfolioAccessError.

---

review.summary: The diff adds fail-fast logging for 403/404 responses from GET /profiles and POST /profiles/transfer, plus a README note. It misses the failure mode the source names first: under isolation, GET /profiles returns *limited results*, not an error. In that case getAccountIDs in each strategy still cannot find the deposit profile and throws the old, misleading "spelt correctly" error. The bot fails to start even when depositing is disabled. The single check only covers a mocked 403 on getProfiles, so a grade of verified overstates what was proven.

concerns.issue: getAccountIDs (around lines 241–275) throws when depositProfileID is missing. It does this unconditionally, even if depositingEnabled is false. With isolation on, GET /profiles likely returns only the key's own portfolio with HTTP 200. The new 403/404 handling never fires, so the user gets the old "Ensure that the depositProfileName is spelt correctly" error and the bot will not start. The diff does not address this most likely isolation symptom. It should at least mention cross portfolio access in that error, and ideally skip the deposit-profile requirement when depositing is disabled.
Same getAccountIDs pattern (around line 255 onward): limited /profiles results cause a misleading startup failure. The diff does not touch it.
Same getAccountIDs pattern (around line 236 onward): limited /profiles results cause a misleading startup failure. The diff does not touch it.

This is a behaviour change beyond the API change: every 403/404 on these two endpoints now skips the previous 3-attempt retry. That includes 403s unrelated to isolation, such as a bad signature, timestamp skew or missing permission. All of them are now labelled as a portfolio-isolation problem, which could misdirect debugging. Consider wording the message as "possibly", or checking the response body.
getFees (line ~152) was named as an affected call site but is unchanged. That is probably fine, since fees are per-key, but the PR does not state that reasoning.

The test covers only a mocked 403 on getProfiles. It does not cover profileTransfer 403/404, the limited-results path, or the strategy-level handling. It also overwrites axios.get globally, sits at the repo root, and is not wired into any test script. The grade of verified rests on this one narrow check.

If profileTransfer now fails fast after a profitable sell, sellPosition's catch only logs it. Positions are still updated correctly, but the user may not notice that profit saving has silently stopped on every cycle. Worth confirming this is acceptable.

checkFirst: Confirm in the Coinbase Exchange docs what GET /profiles returns for a non-cross-portfolio key under isolation (a filtered 200 list or a 403). The quoted source says "limited results", which this diff does not handle.
Check getAccountIDs in all three strategies: with only the trading profile returned, does startup fail with the misleading deposit-profile error?
Decide whether the deposit-profile lookup should be skipped when DEPOSITING_ENABLED=false.
